entries.title: Job 6:3
segments:
Heavier than the sand; very great, insupportable. 
 
  Are swallowed up; are insufficient to express my calamity. 
 
Complaints under calamities, instead of lessening, generally increase them, and unfit the mind to bear them with patience, or receive the benefit they might otherwise occasion.

entries.title: Job 6:4
segments: Arrows of the Almighty; such distresses as God alone can inflict.

entries.title: Job 6:5
segments: Loweth the ox over his fodder? the beast does not complain without reason; nor, as Job contended, did he.

entries.title: Job 6:6
segments: Unsavory be eaten without salt? or, unsavory for want of salt, be eaten?  his calamities are to him as unsavory food, causing bitter complaint.

entries.title: Job 6:7
segments: Trials from which we instinctively shrink in prosperity, sometimes become so wearisome in adversity, that we wish for death.

entries.title: Job 6:8
segments: The thing that I long for; immediate death.

entries.title: Job 6:10
segments:
Harden myself in sorrow; or, exult in sorrow; that is, in the present connection, in the pangs of death. 
 
  Not spare; to cut short my life. 
 
  Not concealed the words of the Holy One; not denied his commands, but made them the rule of my life.

entries.title: Job 6:11
segments:
Should hope; for returning health and prosperity. 
 
  What is mine end; what favorable issue to my present calamities can I look for?

entries.title: Job 6:13
segments: Is not my help in me--wisdom driven quite from me? or, as we may render, "Is it not so that I have no help in me, and counsel is driven quite from me?"

entries.title: Job 6:14
segments:
He forsaketh; he who does not show pity to the afflicted, sins against the Almighty. 
 
The distresses of others should draw forth our compassion and kindness; and the manifestaton of a contrary spirit, is a sin not only against men, but against God.

entries.title: Job 6:15
segments: As a brook; a brook that abounds with water for a time, and then dries away.

entries.title: Job 6:16
segments: The ice; that melted from the mountains.

entries.title: Job 6:19
segments: Tema--Sheba; countries of Arabia.

entries.title: Job 6:20
segments: Hoped; to find water in the channel of the river in the desert.

entries.title: Job 6:21
segments:
Ye are nothing; of no worth to me as comforters, like the brooks that pass away. 
 
Expectations of help from earthly friends are often disappointed; but those which are placed on God will in the end be more than realized.

entries.title: Job 6:22
segments: Did I say, Bring unto me? did he request his friends to help him? All that he had asked of them was comforting words.  But these were denied him.

entries.title: Job 6:25
segments: Right words; words of truth, which, as Job contended, the words of Eliphaz were not.

entries.title: Job 6:27
segments: Overwhelm the fatherless; or, cast lots upon the fatherless; that is, upon his substance, after spoiling him.  He means to say, You exhibit towards me a similar cruelty; for I am in the condition of a fatherless child overwhelmed with sorrow, and without helpers.

entries.title: Job 6:29
segments: Return, I pray you; and address him in a different manner, one that should not impute to him iniquity, but should admit that he was upright and sincere.

entries.title: Job 6:30
segments: Discern; between good and evil in himself.
